description: Fig. 2 is a four-panel composite TEM / TEM-EDS group from an aged 3Cu austenitic low-density steel (Fe-28Mn-10Al-1C-3Cu). (a) Bright-field TEM micrograph with a 50 nm scale bar: numerous dark nanoscale precipitates, roughly equiaxed to short elongated in shape, dispersed in a lighter austenitic matrix. (b) A stacked EDS elemental-mapping block with a 50 nm scale bar in its top greyscale (reference) image, followed by four colour channels labelled Fe (green), Mn (red-brown), Al (yellow) and Cu (cyan); every channel contains the same white dashed rectangle, and two vertical magenta lines bound a second region of interest. (c) HRTEM image (5 nm scale bar) of the irregular-oval Cu-rich phase: two coalesced dark oval particles with no visible interface with the surrounding matrix. (d) HRTEM image (5 nm scale bar) of dark Cu-rich particles plus an inset lattice/FFT image in which yellow arrows and the printed label d = 0.182 nm mark the measured interplanar spacing. Taken together the panels argue that nanoscale Cu-rich precipitates and κ-carbide co-exist in the austenitic matrix and are spatially inter-related.

subfigures.description: Bright-field TEM micrograph of aged 3Cu steel (50 nm scale bar) showing dark nanoscale precipitates in a lighter austenitic matrix; shapes range from equiaxed dots to short bars and irregular ovals. No lattice detail resolvable at this magnification.

Stacked EDS element maps: a top greyscale reference image (50 nm scale bar) over four colour channels labelled Fe (green), Mn (red-brown), Al (yellow) and Cu (cyan). A white dashed rectangle is repeated on every channel and two vertical magenta lines delimit a second zone. Contrast differences between channels are visible; absolute concentrations are not given.

HRTEM image (5 nm scale bar) of the irregular-oval Cu-rich phase; two overlapping dark oval particles embedded in the matrix without an obvious sharp interface. Atomic fringes are faint at the supplied resolution.

HRTEM image (5 nm scale bar) of dark, roughly round/oval Cu-rich particles with an inset lattice (IFFT/FFT) image in the top-right corner; yellow arrows and the text 'd = 0.182nm' annotate the measured lattice spacing. The caption calls this panel the bar-shaped Cu-rich phase, but the particles appear round/oval.

observations.observation: Panel (a) is a bright-field TEM micrograph of the aged 3Cu steel with a 50 nm scale bar, showing dark nanoscale precipitates distributed in a lighter austenitic matrix.
Panel (b) is a stacked EDS mapping block whose channels are labelled Fe (green), Mn (red-brown), Al (yellow) and Cu (cyan), with a 50 nm scale bar in the top reference image.
A white dashed rectangle is drawn at the same location on every EDS channel of panel (b), and two vertical magenta lines mark a second region of interest.
The inset lattice image of panel (d) is annotated with yellow arrows and the printed label 'd = 0.182nm'.
The caption identifies the panels as TEM images of aged 3Cu steel (a), EDS mapping (b), HRTEM image of Cu-rich phase with irregular oval (c) and HRTEM image of Cu-rich phase with bars shapes (d).
The citing text reports that the irregular-oval Cu-rich phase has a diameter of ~10 nm and the bar-shaped Cu-rich phase a length of ~30 nm; these numbers are not printed on the figure.
The citing text states that the Cu-rich phase shows almost no dislocations or stacking faults and that its Cu plane spacing (002) is 0.182 nm, consistent with FCC Cu.
The citing text states that Fe, Mn and Al are brighter inside the white dashed box while Cu is darker there, and that Cu is brighter inside the magenta-line region while Fe, Mn and Al are darker.

The citing text infers the brighter white-dashed-box region to be κ-carbide with Cu excluded outside it, and the brighter magenta-line region to be Cu-rich phase with Fe, Mn and Al excluded outside it.
The citing text states the HR-TEM images show no obvious interface between Cu-rich phase and the austenitic matrix, indicating a coherent relationship.
The citing text gives lattice parameters a = 0.3652 nm for FCC Cu-rich phase, a = 0.3775 nm for κ-carbide and a = 0.3689 nm for the austenitic matrix after solution treatment (XRD).
The caption describes panel (d) as Cu-rich phase with bars shapes, yet the particles visible in (d) at the supplied resolution appear round/oval rather than bar-shaped; both readings are reported.

measured_quantities: lattice/interplanar spacing d (nm) — 0.182 nm printed in panel (d) inset
scale bar length (nm) — 50 nm in (a) and (b), 5 nm in (c) and (d)
precipitate size (nm) — oval diameter ~10 nm and bar length ~30 nm reported by citing text (not printed on figure)
unreadable_items: panel (b): no numeric composition/concentration values or colour-scale bars are shown, so relative EDS intensities cannot be quantified
panel (b): any further annotation inside the white dashed box or between the magenta lines other than the boxes/lines themselves is not legible
panel (c): atomic-plane fringes of the oval Cu-rich phase are too faint to measure an independent d-spacing
